what: GoDaddy sells domain names and the things that come after: website builders, hosting, email, and payment tools for the small businesses that register with it.
customers: Small businesses, sole traders and individuals putting something online, paying annual subscriptions.
money: the growing and more profitable part
website builder, marketing tools and payments
moat: Tens of millions of domains on annual auto-renewal, which renew with almost no effort, and the fact that a domain is where every other service is sold from.
risks: Domain registration growth is slow and the number of customers has been roughly flat
Wix and Squarespace compete directly on website building, and Shopify on commerce
opportunities: $1.7B of free cash flow against a $12.4B market value: about 7 times cash flow
A 17.7% net margin, and revenue grew from $3.8B to $5.0B in four years
Average revenue per customer keeps rising as more buy the higher-priced commerce tools
watch: Annualised recurring revenue and revenue per customer, rather than customer count.
